children: AbbVie, Inc. (NYSE:ABBV) is bolstering its immunology pipeline—acquiring Apogee for zūmi and asthma potential, advancing SKYRIZI and RINVOQ filings, and downplaying DUPIXENT biosimilar risk—while ramping outreach via PGA TOUR sponsorship and a Canada biotech incubator program.
: AbbVie (ABBV) acquired Apogee Therapeutics, adding late‑stage atopic dermatitis drug zumi and potential asthma entry, expanding its immunology portfolio and supporting prior growth targets
: AbbVie (ABBV) expects U.S. approval for SKYRIZI subcutaneous induction in Crohn’s disease in Q4 and anticipates wider payer access in 60–90 days; additional RINVOQ indications are in development.
: AbbVie (ABBV) says it's not highly worried about DUPIXENT biosimilars, citing experience with HUMIRA/STELARA biosimilars and room to grow biologic use in atopic dermatitis globally.
: AbbVie (ABBV) became the PGA TOUR and 2026 Presidents Cup pharma sponsor and launched Birdies for Brain Health, linking PGA TOUR birdies to brain‑health awareness and support.
: AbbVie (ABBV) and BioLabs U of Toronto invite Canada-based early biotech firms to apply by Nov 10, 2026 for one-year free lab/office space, shared equipment, and AbbVie mentorship.
